In [[mathematics]], the '''Hecke algebra''' is the [[algebra over a field|algebra]] generated by [[Hecke operator]]s, which are named after [[Erich Hecke]].

==Properties==
The algebra is a [[commutative ring]].<ref>{{harvnb|Serre|1973|loc=Ch. VII, § 5. Corollary 2.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Bump|1997|loc=Theorem 1.4.2, p. 45.}}</ref>

In the classical [[elliptic modular form]] theory,  the Hecke operators ''T''<sub>''n''</sub> with ''n'' coprime to the level acting on the space of cusp forms of a given weight are [[self-adjoint operator|self-adjoint]] with respect to the [[Petersson inner product]].<ref>{{harvnb|Bump|1997|loc=Theorem 1.4.3, p. 46.}}</ref> Therefore, the [[spectral theorem]] implies that there is a basis of modular forms that are [[eigenfunction]]s for these Hecke operators. Each of these basic forms possesses an [[Euler product]]. More precisely, its [[Mellin transform]] is the [[Dirichlet series]] that has [[Euler product]]s with the local factor for each prime ''p'' is the reciprocal of the '''Hecke polynomial''', a quadratic polynomial in ''p''<sup>&minus;''s''</sup>.<ref>{{harvnb|Serre|1973|loc=Ch. VII, § 5. Corollary 3.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Bump|1997|loc= §1.4, pp. 47–49.}}</ref> In the case treated by Mordell, the space of cusp forms of weight 12 with respect to the full modular group is one-dimensional. It follows that the Ramanujan form has an Euler product and establishes the multiplicativity of ''τ''(''n'').<ref>{{harvnb|Bump|1997|loc= §1.4, p. 49.}}</ref>

==Generalizations==
The classical Hecke algebra has been generalized to other settings, such as the [[Hecke algebra of a locally compact group]] and spherical Hecke algebra that arise when modular forms and other automorphic forms are viewed using [[Adele ring#Automorphic forms|adelic groups]].<ref>{{harvnb|Bump|1997|loc= §2.2, p. 162.}}</ref> These play a central role in the [[Langlands correspondence]].<ref name="Feng-Harris">{{cite arXiv |last1=Feng |first1=Tony |last2=Harris |first2=Michael |author-link2=Michael Harris (mathematician) |date=2024 |title=Derived structures in the Langlands correspondence |class=math.NT |eprint=2409.03035 }}</ref>

The '''derived Hecke algebra''' is a further generalization of Hecke algebras to [[Derived functor|derived functors]].<ref name="Feng-Harris" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Schneider
